Before leaving, run a wash to clear any dirty dishes. When it finishes, unload the dishwasher and let the interior cool. Clean the filter according to the user manual and wipe the door seals with a soft, damp cloth.

For an extended absence, switch off the electricity and close the dishwasher’s water supply valve. Leave the door slightly open if it’s safe to do so. If the cottage could freeze, ask a qualified installer whether the dishwasher should be drained. When you return, restore the supplies and check for leaks before running a wash.

Leave clear instructions for the washer and dryer:

- **Washer:** Check hoses for leaks or damage, turn on the water before washing, follow clothing care labels, and measure detergent for the load and local water hardness. Before leaving, empty the drum, wipe the door seal, switch off the machine and water supply, and leave the door slightly open. Arrange frost protection if the property could freeze.
- **Dryer:** Clean the lint filter after every load, check care labels, and don’t overload the drum. Keep the area around it clear, stay in the property while it runs, and let the full programme—including its cooling stage—finish. Between bookings, make sure the drum is empty and filter clean; switch off and unplug it for an extended vacancy.

If your Corra induction hob flashes a light, switch the zone off before adjusting the pan. Centre it on the zone and check that it’s induction-compatible and that its base is clean and dry. If the light keeps flashing, turn the hob off using its controls, let it cool, and wipe moisture from the control area. If the warning continues, stop using the hob and contact Halvard Home support.

If the display shows a fault message, stop cooking and switch off the hob. Check that the control area is clean and dry, and let hot surfaces cool before wiping them. If the isolator is safely accessible, switch the hob off there for 60 seconds, then restore power. If the message returns, leave the hob off and contact support; don’t remove the glass or attempt internal repairs.

Stop the programme, switch off the dryer, unplug it, and let it cool. Clean and refit the lint filter, empty and refit the water tank if your model has one, and check that nothing is caught in the door. Reconnect the dryer and try the programme again. If the warning keeps flashing, stop using it and contact Halvard Home support, describing which light flashes and when.

If you find ice inside your Tessa dishwasher, don’t start a programme. Switch it off and contact Halvard Home support for advice before using it again. Don’t use boiling water or sharp tools to remove the ice, as they can damage the dishwasher.

Stop the dryer immediately. Switch it off and unplug it from the wall only if it’s safe; don’t run another cycle to test it.

If you see smoke or flames, keep the door closed, leave the property and call 999. Don’t use water or try to move the dryer. If there’s no sign of fire, leave it unplugged until it cools completely. You can then clear the lint filter and check that the external vents are unobstructed—but don’t use the dryer again until a qualified appliance technician has checked it.

Use the heating schedule to set a later **start time**, rather than choosing a delay duration. For example, if you want heating to start one hour after 18:00, schedule it for 19:00. Set your target temperature, save the schedule, and check that it’s enabled for the correct day. Heating will only start if the room is cooler than the target temperature.

If your cooker hood’s display is blank, check that its wall switch or fused spur is on, then try the light and fan controls to see whether the whole hood has lost power. Switch off the electrical supply for 60 seconds, then turn it back on and try again.

If the fan and light work but the screen is still blank, contact Halvard Home support and tell them which controls respond. If nothing works, check whether other kitchen appliances have power. Don’t remove covers or touch internal wiring; arrange a qualified inspection if the problem continues.
Keep the cooker hood running for 10 minutes after cooking to clear lingering steam and smells.

To update your appliance’s built-in programming (firmware), the steps depend on the model:

- **Tessa dishwasher:** Make sure it’s on home Wi-Fi, switched on, empty, and not running a wash programme. On the control panel, go to **Settings > Firmware update > Check for updates**. Select **Install** if an update is available. Keep the dishwasher powered and connected to Wi-Fi until the display confirms completion.
- **Keel washing machine:** Finish the wash, empty the drum, and leave the machine switched on and connected to Wi-Fi. In the Halvard Home app, select your machine and go to **Settings > Firmware update**. Tap **Install** if an update is available. Don’t switch it off, unplug it, or restart your router during installation; wait for the app’s completion confirmation.
- **Ashby tumble dryer:** Finish the drying programme, empty the drum, and leave the dryer on and connected to Wi-Fi. On the display, go to **Settings > Software update > Check for updates**, then select **Install** if one is available. Keep it powered until the display confirms completion.

If an update fails, check the Wi-Fi connection and try again. Contact Halvard Home support if it continues to fail.

It depends on the device. The Lumen thermostat factory reset clears saved Wi‑Fi details, heating schedules, and personal settings, so you’ll need to reconnect to Wi‑Fi and set your preferences again. The Orrin heat pump reset clears saved schedules and temperature preferences; the passage doesn’t say whether it removes wireless login information.

If your heating controller isn’t appearing in the companion app, check that it’s powered on and your phone is connected to your home Wi‑Fi. Then:

1. Move your phone close to the controller.
2. Turn on Bluetooth and allow the app any requested Bluetooth, nearby-device, or local-network permissions.
3. Turn your phone’s Wi‑Fi off for 10 seconds, then back on.
4. Close the app completely, reopen it, and try adding the controller again.
5. Check for an app update.

If it still doesn’t appear, restart your phone and contact support with your phone model and what happens during setup. Avoid factory resetting the controller.

Warm, moist cooking air can condense on the extractor’s cold surfaces, especially in winter or when the duct runs through an unheated space. Use the hood while cooking and for 10 minutes afterwards, and keep kitchen ventilation openings clear. If you see frost, don’t chip it off or apply direct heat; have a qualified installer check the duct insulation and outside vent.

Switch off the washer at the socket and unplug it, then turn off the water supply and disconnect the inlet hose. Drain any remaining water safely, empty and dry the drum, and secure the hoses and cable so they won’t drag or stretch. Refit the original transit bolts according to the manual; if they’re missing, contact Halvard Home before moving it. Keep the washer upright and use two people to move it. At the new house, remove the bolts before using the washer.

If your Keel washer shows an error code, stop the programme and note the exact message. Switch it off and unplug it for five minutes, handling the plug only with dry hands. Check that the door is fully closed and no clothing is caught in the seal; don’t force the door open if water remains inside. If the fault returns, stop using the washer and contact Halvard Home support with the message and when it appeared.

Warm, moist air may be getting into the fridge freezer, where it condenses and freezes. Frequent door opening, uncovered food, a poor door seal, or something preventing the door from closing fully can contribute. Check the seals and keep food covered and vents clear.

For your Mira robot vacuum, place it on its plugged-in charging dock. Hold the **Power** and **Home** buttons together for 10 seconds, releasing them when you hear the reset announcement. Leave it on the dock while it restarts. Then add it again in the Halvard Home app and reconnect it to Wi‑Fi.

The reset removes saved Wi‑Fi details, cleaning schedules, and maps, so you’ll need to set those up again.

The passages cover two types of heating equipment:

- **Orrin heat pump:** Don’t put it in household rubbish or your household recycling bin. Have a qualified heat pump installer disconnect it and safely recover the refrigerant. Then ask your replacement installer about collection, or check with your council for a service that accepts heat pumps. Confirm arrangements before moving it; keep it upright while awaiting collection and use a licensed waste carrier if transporting it yourself.
- **Lumen smart thermostat:** Recycle it as electrical waste at a centre that accepts small electrical appliances. If it’s wired in, have a qualified electrician or heating engineer disconnect it. Reset it and remove it from your smart home account if it still works; recycle user-removable batteries separately.

Check the power supply first: make sure the plug is fully inserted and the wall socket is switched on. You can test the socket with a working lamp. If the socket works, unplug the dryer briefly, reconnect it, close the door firmly, and try again. If the plug or cable is damaged, smells burnt, or feels unusually hot, stop using the dryer and contact Halvard Home support.
Your refrigerator needs a **2.4 GHz Wi‑Fi network**.

For a cozy home with lower electricity use:

- Set your heating to about **19°C**, then adjust to a comfortable temperature. Lowering it by 1°C may reduce energy use, as long as everyone stays warm enough.
- Use a heating schedule that fits your routine. For a heat pump, keep temperatures fairly steady and try a small overnight reduction rather than switching it off. If you’re away, use a holiday setting or a lower temperature, and keep the heat pump connected to power in cold weather.
- Avoid turning the thermostat sharply higher to warm rooms faster; it generally won’t make them heat faster. Keep furniture and curtains clear of the thermostat.
- On the hob, use the lowest setting that cooks your food, turn it down to a simmer once water boils, and use a lid where possible.
- Set your fridge to **4°C** and freezer to **−18°C**; keep doors closed and avoid blocking air vents.

Don’t change hot-water hygiene settings just to save energy, and follow your installer’s advice if you’re unsure what temperature is suitable for your home.

Switch off the Mira robot vacuum and remove it from its charging dock. Check the lid’s opening, hinges and catch for dust, hair or small objects, and wipe the accessible edges with a dry, soft cloth. Make sure the dust bin is seated correctly and nothing sticks up above it. Lower the lid gently—don’t force it. If it still won’t stay down or a hinge or catch looks damaged, stop using the vacuum and contact Halvard Home support.
First, check that the cooker hood’s wall switch or fused connection switch is on. If it has a plug, make sure it’s fully inserted—only if you can reach it safely.

Unplug the kettle and let it cool completely, then empty it. Use a descaler labelled as suitable for kettles, following its instructions for the amount, water temperature, and treatment time. Don’t exceed the kettle’s maximum-fill mark or mix cleaning products.

Afterward, empty and rinse the kettle thoroughly. Fill it to the maximum mark, boil the water, and discard it; repeat once before making drinks. Keep the base, plug, and outside dry, and never immerse the kettle in water.

For the Vale fridge freezer, first check that food, bottles or packaging aren’t blocking the door, and push drawers fully in and shelves into their supports. Clean and dry the rubber seal and the surface it touches, and check for ice stopping the door from closing—don’t chip ice with a sharp tool. Don’t force the door shut. If it still hangs unevenly or the seal is split, contact Halvard Home support.

Switch off and unplug the tea maker, then let it cool completely. If the plug or socket is wet, don’t touch it—switch off the electricity at the consumer unit first. Lift the kettle off its base and dry the outside. Check whether water ran down from the spout or lid, and make sure it wasn’t filled above the MAX mark. If you see cracks or the leak continues, stop using it and contact Halvard Home support. Don’t immerse the electrical base or attempt repairs yourself.

First check the controller’s power supply: make sure its clearly labelled switch is on. If it already is, switch it off, wait 30 seconds, then turn it back on. Don’t remove the cover or touch wiring. If other nearby electrical items have also lost power, there may be a wider power cut.

For a **Tessa dishwasher**, connect it to your home Wi‑Fi, make sure no wash programme is running, empty it and leave it switched on. On the control panel, go to **Settings > Firmware update > Check for updates**. If an update is available, select **Install** and follow the display instructions. Keep the dishwasher powered on and connected to Wi‑Fi until the display confirms the update is complete.

Pause the programme and wait for the drum to stop. If the door unlocks, spread heavy items evenly around the drum and restart the programme—never force the door open. Check that the machine is on a hard, level floor, with all four feet touching and no rocking. If it was newly installed, check the installation guide to make sure the transport bolts were removed. If strong vibration continues, stop using the machine and contact Halvard Home support.

Stop the cycle and turn off the water supply tap. Switch off and unplug the machine only if the plug and surrounding area are dry—never touch a wet plug or socket.

When it’s safe, wipe up the water and check visible inlet hose connections, whether the drain hose has slipped out, and whether water is running down from the detergent drawer. Don’t run another cycle while the leak is unexplained. If the hoses seem secure or the water is coming from beneath the casing, contact Halvard Home support.

Stop cleaning and switch off the vacuum. If the charging dock or plug is wet, switch off the mains socket before handling it.

Remove the water tank and empty it over a sink. Check that the filler cap is fully closed and inspect the tank and outlet for cracks. Dry the tank and the vacuum’s underside with a cloth; don’t rinse the vacuum body or put it back on the dock while wet.

If the tank is cracked or water leaks again after you refit it securely, stop using the mopping function and contact Halvard Home support.

Make sure the heat pump is switched on and your phone is connected to your home Wi‑Fi. Then try these steps in order:

1. Move your phone closer to the heat pump.
2. Allow the app any requested Bluetooth or local network access in your phone settings.
3. Turn your phone’s Wi‑Fi off for 10 seconds, then back on.
4. Close and reopen the app, then try adding the heat pump again.
5. Check the app store for an update.

If the heat pump still doesn’t appear, contact Halvard Home support and tell them your phone model and what happens when you try to connect.

Check that the washing machine is switched on and your phone is nearby. Connect your phone to a **2.4 GHz Wi‑Fi network** (5 GHz won’t work for setup), turn on Bluetooth, and allow the app to access nearby devices. Close and reopen the app, then try adding the machine again and follow the in-app pairing instructions.

If it still doesn’t appear, restart your phone and router and try again once Wi‑Fi is available. If the problem continues, contact Halvard Home support with your phone model and a description of where setup stops.

Yes. Water beneath the outdoor unit during or shortly after defrosting is usually normal: ice on the outdoor coil melts and drains away. Monitor it to see whether it stops. If water runs continuously or comes from elsewhere, arrange an inspection by a qualified heat pump engineer.

Orrin heat pumps warm rooms gradually, and they typically run at lower heating-water temperatures than boilers. As a result, the radiators may feel cooler even when the system is heating normally. Cold weather and defrost cycles can temporarily slow heating further.
The Fenwick cooker hood needs a 2.4 GHz home Wi-Fi network. It cannot connect to a network set to 5 GHz only.
No. The Halvard Home Brio kettle has no timer or delay-start setting; you need to switch it on manually when you’re ready to boil water.

Yes. A gentle rumbling or hissing sound while the kettle heats is usually normal. A click when it switches off is expected too. If the noise is sudden or unusually loud, or comes with leaking, a burning smell or visible damage, stop using the kettle and contact Halvard Home support.

Common causes include loose items such as coins or keys, metal zips or buttons hitting the drum, an uneven load, or the dryer touching nearby furniture.

Stop the programme, switch off and unplug the dryer, and let the drum cool before checking. Remove the laundry and loose items, redistribute bulky items, and make sure the dryer stands level and does not touch a wall or cupboard. Don’t reach underneath or remove panels. If the noise continues or you hear loud grinding, stop using the dryer and contact Halvard Home support.

Switch off and unplug the machine, and let any hot water cool completely. Open the lower-front filter flap with towels and a shallow tray underneath. Slowly loosen the filter to drain trapped water, then remove and clear away debris. Rinse the filter, wipe the opening, and refit it securely without forcing it. Close the flap, reconnect power, and run a short rinse to check for leaks. If draining is still slow or you notice a leak, stop using the machine and contact Halvard Home support.

Switch the dryer off at the socket before unplugging it. Use a torch to check the area. If it’s safe to open the door, carefully remove the laundry—it may be hot—and spread it out so heat can escape.

When the electricity supply is stable, reconnect the dryer, check the laundry and restart a suitable programme if more drying is needed. If you notice a burning smell or visible damage, leave it unplugged and contact Halvard Home support.

Make sure the dishwasher is switched on and your phone is connected to your home Wi‑Fi. Then:

1. Move your phone close to the dishwasher.
2. Turn on Bluetooth and allow the app any nearby-device or location permissions it requests.
3. Avoid a guest Wi‑Fi network.
4. Close and reopen the app, then try adding the dishwasher again.
5. If it still isn’t found, switch the dishwasher off at the mains for 30 seconds, then switch it back on.

If the problem continues, contact Halvard Home support and tell them which steps you’ve tried.

Water underneath your Vale fridge freezer may be from a spill, a blocked defrost drain, or a door that isn’t closing properly. Check that food or packaging isn’t stopping the doors from closing, and gently clear any loose debris around a visible drain hole. If the leak returns, contact Halvard Home support.

A rattling or banging noise can be caused by loose objects in the drum, an uneven load, or the machine not being level. Pause the programme and wait for the drum to stop and the door to unlock—don’t force it open. Spread heavy items evenly, check for coins, keys or other loose objects, and see whether the machine rocks when gently pressed at a corner. If it does, switch it off and unplug it before adjusting the feet. For a newly installed machine, check the installation guide to make sure the transit bolts have been removed. If you hear grinding, smell burning or notice a leak, stop using it and contact Halvard Home support.

To factory reset your Orrin heat pump:

1. Note your heating schedules and temperature preferences—the reset will erase them.
2. Make sure the heat pump is switched on and showing no warning.
3. On the controller, open **Settings** → **System** → **Factory reset**.
4. Select **Confirm** and leave the power connected while the controller restarts.
5. When the home screen returns, check the date and time, then re-enter your preferred temperatures and schedule.

If **Factory reset** is unavailable or the controller does not restart, contact Halvard Home support. Do not open the unit or change installer settings to force a reset.
Your old Halvard Home Corra induction hob should be recycled as electrical equipment, not placed in your household rubbish bin.

To switch the child lock **on**, make sure the kettle is not heating, then press and hold the lock button for **three seconds**. The indicator lights up when the controls are locked.

To switch it **off**, press and hold the same button for **three seconds**, until the indicator goes out. The lock doesn’t lock the lid or make hot water safe to handle, so keep the kettle and cable out of children’s reach and supervise children around it.

Connect the fridge freezer to your home Wi-Fi and make sure it has a steady power supply. On the control panel, open **Settings**, select **Software update**, then choose **Check for updates**. If an update is available, follow the on-screen instructions.

Keep the appliance switched on and don’t unplug or restart it while the update installs. Keep the doors closed as much as possible, and wait for the control panel to confirm completion. If the update fails, check your Wi-Fi connection before trying again.

First, make sure the kettle has finished boiling and cooled down; don’t reset it while it’s heating.

1. Place the kettle securely on its base.
2. Plug in the base and switch on the wall socket.
3. Press and hold the power button for 10 seconds.
4. Release it when the indicator light flashes twice. The flashes confirm the reset is complete.

You can then choose your settings again. If the light doesn’t flash, check that the kettle is seated correctly and repeat the steps.

If the outside of your Keel feels damp, wipe it with a soft, dry cloth and improve ventilation. Check nearby hoses and connections; recurring puddles may indicate a leak.

If you notice frost, stop using the machine. Switch it off and unplug it only if your hands, plug and socket are dry. Let the machine and room warm naturally—don’t use boiling water, a hairdryer or a heater. Once thawed, check for visible leaks. If frost returns or you find damaged hoses, contact Halvard Home support before running another wash.

Unplug the kettle and let it cool completely. Empty it, open the lid, and gently remove the filter from behind the spout—don’t force it if it’s stuck. Rinse it under warm running water and use a soft brush to loosen limescale. For stubborn deposits, soak the filter in warm water for 10 minutes, then brush gently and rinse thoroughly. Refit it securely before using the kettle.

Avoid abrasive cleaners and metal brushes, and never immerse the kettle body, base, or plug in water.

To factory-reset your Corra induction hob:

1. Remove all cookware, let the cooking zones cool, and make sure the control panel is clean and dry.
2. Switch the hob off with the power button, but leave its electrical supply connected.
3. Press and hold the **timer** and **minus** buttons together for five seconds.
4. Release them when you hear a beep.
5. Press the power button once to confirm the reset.

Switch the hob on again and set your preferences. If the controls do not respond or the reset does not complete, contact Halvard Home support. Do not remove the hob or open its casing.

Make sure the hob has power and your phone is nearby. Turn on Bluetooth and Wi‑Fi, and allow the Halvard Home app access to Bluetooth and nearby devices (and local network access if prompted). Then fully close the app for 30 seconds, reopen it, put the hob into pairing mode as instructed in the app, and search again.

If the hob was previously connected, check whether it’s listed under another account or home. If it still isn’t found, contact Halvard Home support and tell them your phone model and where setup stops.

To switch the child lock **on**, press and hold the padlock button for three seconds. The padlock light will come on. Any wash already in progress will continue.

To switch it **off**, press and hold the same button for three seconds. Wait for the padlock light to go out before choosing a programme or changing a setting.

The lock disables the controls but does not lock the door. Keep children away while the dishwasher is running, as opening the door can release hot steam, and store detergent out of their reach.

Unusual or stronger-than-normal vibration can be caused by something touching the unit, loose mounting points, or an uneven base.

Switch the heat pump off using its normal controls. Remove loose items touching the casing and clear leaves or debris around the outdoor unit. Don’t remove covers, reach through the grille, or adjust mounting bolts. If there’s no visible damage, restart it and listen from a safe distance.

If the vibration continues, switch it off and contact Halvard Home support or a qualified installer. Keep it off if it shakes violently, moves on its base, or makes a grinding noise.

Yes. A loose wall fixing or nearby heating equipment may be causing the vibration rather than the thermostat itself. If the heating is running, switch it off using the thermostat and wait five minutes to see whether the vibration stops. Don’t pull the thermostat away from the wall or try to tighten hidden fixings.
A 3-hour delay means the washing machine waits 3 hours before the wash begins. It does **not** mean the wash will finish in 3 hours.

Switch off the washing machine, unplug it, and turn off the water supply. Check the rubber seal for splits, holes, or places it has pulled away. **Do not use the machine if the seal is torn or leaking.**

Contact Halvard Home support with your machine’s model details and a clear photo of the damage. Ask them to confirm the replacement seal fits your machine before ordering. Have a qualified repair technician fit it, since a poorly fitted seal can leak.

Finish any wash programme, empty the drum and leave the machine switched on. Make sure it’s connected to your home Wi-Fi, then in the Halvard Home app select your Keel washing machine and go to **Settings > Firmware update**. Tap **Install** if an update is available and follow the instructions.

Keep the machine switched on, and don’t unplug it or restart your router while the update is running. Wait for the app to confirm completion before using the machine; you can’t start a wash during installation.

First add your Keel washing machine to the Halvard Home app and confirm it appears online. Then:

1. Open your voice assistant’s app and go to the section for adding devices, skills or services.
2. Search for and select **Halvard Home**.
3. Sign in using the same Halvard Home account you use for the washing machine.
4. Allow account linking, then ask the assistant to discover devices.
5. Give the machine a simple name, such as “Washing machine,” so the assistant can recognize it.

If pairing fails, check your internet connection and make sure the machine is still online in the Halvard Home app before trying again.

Make sure the hood has power and your phone is connected to your home Wi‑Fi, not mobile data. Move your phone within one metre of the hood, switch the hood off at the wall for 30 seconds and back on, then enable Bluetooth and allow the app’s nearby-device or local-network permissions. Put the hood into pairing mode as described in its user guide and try adding it again.

If it still doesn’t appear, restart your phone and router. Contact Halvard Home support if the problem continues.

Make sure Mira is switched on and near your router. Connect your phone to a **2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network** (5 GHz alone won’t work), turn on Bluetooth, and allow the app access to nearby devices. Close and reopen the Halvard Home app, then try adding Mira again.

If it still isn’t found, restart your phone and router and repeat setup. Avoid a factory reset unless Halvard Home support advises it. Contact support if these steps don’t help.

Check that the fridge freezer is switched on and your phone is connected to your home Wi‑Fi. Move closer to the appliance, turn on Bluetooth, and allow any nearby-device or local-network permissions the app requests. Follow the pairing instructions in the guide, then fully close the app, wait 10 seconds, reopen it, and try adding the appliance again.

If it still isn’t found, check for an app update. If the problem continues, contact Halvard Home support and tell them which steps you’ve tried.
Wait 7 minutes before cleaning the Tessa dishwasher. If any surfaces are still hot, let them cool until they’re safe to touch.
Wait **45 hours** after moving your Lumen smart thermostat before switching it on. Make sure it has been checked for damage and safely installed first.
An Ashby tumble dryer is inspected within **26 days of arrival**.
You would pay **£38.00** for the fault diagnosis if no repair follows. The charge also applies if you decline a quoted repair; Halvard Home will explain when booking whether it applies.
Wait **111 minutes** for the Ashby tumble dryer to cool before cleaning it.
Wait until the kettle has cooled completely before cleaning it. The safety instructions specify 36 minutes; if it still feels hot after that, wait longer.
A warranty repair will be completed within **37 working days** of the fault being confirmed.
A regular service usually takes about **230 minutes**.
A warranty repair is completed within **34 working days** of the fault being confirmed.
The warranty lasts **45 months from the date the thermostat is delivered**.

Have the Ashby tumble dryer safety-checked every **27 months**, through Halvard Home or a suitably qualified appliance technician. This scheduled check doesn’t replace stopping use and seeking advice if you notice a fault or damage.
